Incise

in-SIZE · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To incise to carve or cut into a surface.

The engraver carefully incised the family crest into the silver ring.

Worked Example

Ancient scribes would incise their records into wet clay tablets, letting them harden into a permanent copy.

Incise describes a precise, controlled kind of cutting -- carving a mark, letter, or design into a surface, usually with a fine tool.

How Incise Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

carve

carve: cut a design into a material

engrave

engrave: cut letters or designs onto a hard surface

Antonyms

smooth

smooth: make a surface even and unmarked

erase

erase: rub out a mark completely

How Strong Is It? — scratch → incise → gouge

scratch vs. incise

scratch vs. incise: A scratch is a shallow, often accidental mark on a surface.

gouge vs. incise

gouge vs. incise: To gouge something is to tear out a deep, rough chunk of it, far more violent than a controlled incision.

Put it together

Put it together: in- ("into") + cis ("to cut") + -e (verb ending) = to cut into.

Use the root in a new word: incisor

Use the root in a new word: incisor: The same root gives us "incisor," the flat front tooth designed for cutting into food.
